selection_rationale: cand-2026-netops-1 most directly addresses the programme mandate (operational reliability of LLM-produced NetOps artifacts) with a falsifiable, paired design (single-shot vs verifier-assisted generate–validate–repair), strong venue relevance, and feasible compute needs. It yields clear primary outcomes (verifier pass-rate delta), aligns with established gaps (verifier-driven end-to-end evaluation), and the critic review reached a pass verdict after identifying reparable design issues.
unresolved_uncertainties: External validity: how well synthetic/public topologies and policies map to production networks (affects generalizability).
Hosted-model nondeterminism and provider-rate/price constraints (may affect paired comparisons and required retries).
Verifier correctness and specification risk (bugs or incomplete assertions could bias pass/fail labels).
Availability of provider-exposed internals (log-probs) that could enable richer diagnostics or secondary analyses.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Publish provenance and public-release plan for the synthetic corpus with diverse topology/policy strata.
Implement and independently validate a verifier test-suite (unit tests, canonical cases) to ensure correctness of pass/fail labels.
Pre-register sample-size and power analysis for the paired comparison (McNemar or equivalent) and the retry policy to handle LLM nondeterminism.
Record and freeze full prompt templates, model/version identifiers, seeds/configs (where provider allows), and include them in the Disclosure Statement.
Define and document operational strata for analysis (topology size, policy types) and planned subgroup/sample allocation to support stratified inference.
